[H1]Active Senate[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Under some types of government ([LINK=CIVIC_REPRESENTATION]Representation[\\LINK], [LINK=CIVIC_UNIVERSAL_SUFFRAGE]Universal Suffrage[\\LINK]), the Senate can interfere with your military policy. Thus, it may invalidate your declarations of war and/or force you to sign a peace treaty with your enemies.[PARAGRAPH:2]The decisions of the Senate depend in particular on the scale of the conflict, either potential or actual, and its real interest. Thus, pursue a policy military under democratic regime becomes more difficult.[PARAGRAPH:2] However, when an opponent make unpleasant acts to your nation, by a embargo, a negative vote, an espionage mission, etc. ..., you have a sufficient pretext to go to war without Senate intervention. Any war pretext is valid for one turn and throughout the conflict in case of a declaration of war. Of course, malicious acts of enemies who are already at war against you are a pretext to circumvent the Senate.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]

[H1]Condamned Civic[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]The United Nations can vote on resolution of condemnation of a civic. If and only if this civic is adopted by one of the voting players. Are condemnable by the United Nations, some of the most extremist civics. [PARAGRAPH:2]Choosing a condemned civic generate a diplomatic penalty from the voting members and exclude the civilization to the clan of members which can vote, which in itself is not always a bad thing (as you assess the risks and benefits of such a situation.)[PARAGRAPH:2]It is possible that a AI player proposes such a resolution and pass it, in which case it can influence the course of the game. But from a human point of view, the interest is more subtile. It allows to turn some civilizations against another. Indeed, if you want to attack an opponent who has a state religion shared by you and your allies, but he chose a different religious doctrine, you can try to condemn it to make it a pariat and attack without offending your brothers in faith, even with their assistance.[PARAGRAPH:2]From a historical point of view, the interest is basically to be able to condemn the reform among others.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]
